Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors: Fatigue and low mood with long-standing decreased energy; reduced appetite with gradual weight loss (~1 stone over ~6 months); headaches and intermittent nausea; shortness of breath or palpitations in confined spaces (e.g., lifts); work stress after changing law firms; limited physical activity noted (haven’t been walking recently). Noted history of hypothyroidism with prior thyroxine therapy, currently not taking it since changing doctors.

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Working impression: Multisystem symptom cluster including fatigue, low mood, appetite loss, weight loss, and episodic palpitations with dyspnea; possible thyroid dysfunction due to non-adherence; anemia and other endocrine/metabolic processes considered. No urgent red flags identified in history; plan prioritizes baseline labs and subsequent evaluation.
- Relevant differential diagnoses (aligned with transcript and DDx):
  - Major depressive disorder with somatic symptoms
    - Likelihood: High
    - Rationale: Months of low mood, low energy, appetite loss, and weight loss with work/home stressors; somatic symptoms (headache, nausea) common in depression
  - Hypothyroidism due to non-adherence to thyroxine
    - Likelihood: Medium-High
    - Rationale: History of hypothyroidism with lapse in thyroxine therapy; fatigue and weight changes could reflect thyroid status
    - Note: Conflict noted — weight loss is less typical of hypothyroidism (usually weight gain); palpitations are more typical of hyperthyroidism, though can occur with thyroid dysfunction or anxiety
  - Anemia (iron-deficiency or other)
    - Likelihood: Medium
    - Rationale: Fatigue and headaches; weight/appetite changes could accompany chronic disease or iron deficiency
  - Anxiety/panic symptoms with somatic manifestations
    - Likelihood: Medium
    - Rationale: Palpitations and dyspnea in confined spaces (lifts); work-related stress and mood concerns
- Priority and plan: Obtain general blood work to assess for anemia, renal and hepatic function, vitamin levels; assess thyroid status indirectly via prior history and current non-adherence; if results are unrevealing, consider targeted examination; monitor for chest pain or bowel changes (red flags) and contact care team if symptoms worsen
- Conflicts/uncertainties: See above note on hypothyroidism weight-change mismatch; transcript and DDx disagree on typical thyroid weight effects

Management Plan

- Immediate actions: Arrange general blood tests (complete blood count for anemia, renal function, liver function, vitamin levels); no urgent physical examination indicated at this time
- Follow-up and monitoring: After blood results, determine need for physical examination; patient to contact support to arrange blood draw; results will trigger a text-based appointment booking; if symptoms worsen (chest pain, new bowel changes) contact care team urgently
- Patient education: If chest pains occur, go to emergency department; contact app support for scheduling; maintain awareness of red-flag symptoms and seek care accordingly

- Reproductive or sexual health clinic referral: Not recorded
- Mental health support if indicated (e.g., psychologist, AMS support): Not recorded
- CTG registration: Not recorded
- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test): Not recorded

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Major depressive disorder with somatic symptoms
  - Justification: Months of low mood, low energy, appetite loss, weight loss, and work stress; somatic symptoms (headache, nausea)
  - Likelihood: High
- Hypothyroidism due to non-adherence to thyroxine
  - Justification: History of hypothyroidism, current non-adherence; fatigue and weight changes
  - Likelihood: Medium-High
  - Conflict noted: Weight loss is not typical for hypothyroidism (weight gain more common) per DDx
- Anemia (iron-deficiency or other)
  - Justification: Fatigue, headaches; weight/appetite changes could accompany chronic illness; SBP/functional capacity preserved but exertional fatigue possible
  - Likelihood: Medium

Quality checks (bottom of note)

- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Blood pressure, BMI, and formal vitals are not recorded
  - Immunisation status reviewed: Not recorded
  - Mental health screening or self-harm risk assessment performed: Not documented
  - Alcohol/tobacco/substance use history: Not recorded
  - Sexual health and cervical/ STI screening details: Not recorded
- Internal contradictions between transcript and DDx:
  - Conflict noted: Weight loss in the transcript vs DDx note that hypothyroidism typically presents with weight gain
- Transcript quality comment:
  - Some questions and responses were brief or ambiguous (e.g., mood details and exact onset); telemedicine format limited detailed objective data (e.g., vitals, objective exam). The plan appropriately relies on baseline blood tests to guide next steps.
